title: Karta Polaka Interview: Language, Topics and How to Prepare
excerpt: The Karta Polaka interview is a conversation in Polish about language and traditions. What 'basic Polish' means, topics, phrases and a prep plan.
metaDescription: The Karta Polaka interview is a conversation in Polish about language and traditions. What 'basic Polish' means, topics, phrases and a prep plan.
summary: The Karta Polaka confirms belonging to the Polish Nation; it is free, decided by the consul, and is not Polish citizenship.

Unless you have a state certificate or a Polish-language school or university certificate, the consul assesses your Polish in a conversation held in Polish that also covers Polish traditions and customs.
The Act asks for 'at least basic knowledge' of Polish and names no CEFR level; aiming for a comfortable A2 gives you a safety margin.
Prepare your family history, your reasons for applying, Wigilia and Wielkanoc customs, 3 May and 11 November, the national symbols and a basic outline of Polish history.

factNotes: No official question list, format or score for the consul's conversation exists, so topics are presented as our suggestions built from the official 'traditions and customs' wording; the sample dialogue is labelled as illustrative. The A2 target is explicitly framed as our advice (the Act gives no CEFR level). The 'before 2019 only former Soviet states' line rests on the 2019 amending act (which rewrote art. 2(2) and repealed art. 2(4)) plus press coverage of the earlier 15-country scope; the original country list itself was not re-read. Left out: renewal timing (gov.pl says apply at least 3 months before expiry; the Act says not earlier than 6 months before, so I only say 'can be renewed'), the list of countries for which a voivode handles applications (regulation not opened), appeal deadlines, cash-benefit amounts, and any '2023 changes' (no Karta Polaka amendment found in 2023; later amending acts of 2022 and 2025 only touch work-permit cross-references). 'Decision within two months' is quoted from a consulate page and hedged as 'normally'. Historical/cultural facts (966, 1791, 1918, partitions, anthem first line, Wigilia/Easter customs) are standard and match the linked PolishPal posts.
